tooling.message:
feat: the change scope decides what hooks and CI run

## Intent

Hooks and CI ran every check and build whatever a commit changed. A change of only the plan needs no checks at all, and a change of only docs needs only site work. This should be decided in one central place for every repo, not in each repo on its own.

## Key changes

- A classifier, `lernapps changes`, names the scope: none for only .vibe/**, docs for only docs/**/*.md (with or without the plan), all for anything else or when the changed files cannot be known.
- The lists are allowlists with a default per kind of repo (app, tooling, site); a repo may declare exceptions in package.json, and invalid entries fail.
- lernapps check --pre-commit and --pre-push ask it first: with none, and with docs in an app, they print one line and check nothing; with docs in a repo with a site, only the site is built and checked. The tooling's own heavy-test gating uses the same patterns.
- The app-check and app-publish actions classify the event themselves, so generated apps skip plan-only and docs-only changes with no configuration.
- A reusable workflow outputs the scope; each workflow gates its jobs on it and has one always-running final job as the required check, since a check skipped by a workflow path filter would stay pending.
- The generated publish workflow drops its paths-ignore for .vibe.
- The classifier's tests ignore a hook's git variables and give git a timeout, so they also pass under the pre-push hook and on a busy machine.

moved.why: A test fix inside tooling#57, the change-scope classifier.
